correctness.rationale: PASS. The K3^[2] Fujiki polarization was reconstructed independently. For q(H)=4, q(delta)=-2, alpha=H-s delta, beta=H-t delta and the Hilbert-Chow divisor class proportional to delta, the divisor condition is q(alpha)q(delta,beta)-2q(alpha,beta)q(alpha,delta)<=0. Its equality locus is t s^2-4s+2t=0; for t=1/2 the small root is 4-sqrt(14)=0.2583426132..., strictly inside (0,1/2), and for general t=1/k it is irrational and lies in (0,t). The sign changes across this root, while every integral BBF hyperplane meets the (H,delta)-plane on a rational ray. The endpoint alpha=beta is uniformly slope J-stable because every proper m-dimensional subvariety has slope m<4. Thus the same ample MBM chamber contains a stable point and points destabilized by E. What is proved is the slope/subvariety statement; no analytic J-equation wall is claimed.
